spec.name: rmsnorm_qwen2_5_0p5b
spec.description: RMSNorm over a row of 896 activations: sum of squares, one inverse square root, and a scaled product per element, requantized to int8

derivation.rule: row length from d_model; the rsqrt input and shift widths from that block's ports; the extra shift k from the bound |t| < 2**(data_width+ow-k) against the requantizer input

ports.name: eps
ports.desc: epsilon, in units of the sum of squares

ports.name: o_valid
ports.desc: a normalised element is on o_data

behavior: start is a one-cycle pulse, with eps, scale_o and shift_o held stable for the whole row. busy must be high on the clock edge that samples start, so it already reads 1 one cycle later, and it stays high until the last output is emitted.

x_data and g_data are registered reads: each carries the element at address a on the cycle after x_addr or g_addr = a. If the address is itself a register, that is two clock edges after the edge that loads a into it.
Pass 1: ssq = eps + sum over i in 0..895 of x_i * x_i, an unsigned 30-bit value held in a register named ssq. Start the sum from eps, not from zero.
Then (m, e) = rsqrt(ssq) from the supplied rsqrt block, held in registers named rs_m ([16:0]) and rs_e ([4:0]).

Pass 2: for i in 0..895, t_i = (x_i * g_i * m) >>> (e + 0), an arithmetic shift of the signed product, which floors. Then o_i = requant(t_i, scale_o, shift_o): multiply by scale_o, add 2**(shift_o-1) when shift_o > 0, arithmetic shift right by shift_o, saturate to [-128, 127]. |t_i| stays under 2**25, so it fits the requantizer's 29-bit input.
Emit each o_i with o_index = i and o_valid high for exactly that one cycle. Outputs may come in any order, but each index exactly once, and o_valid must be low at every other time.
The testbench reads ssq, rs_m and rs_e directly to check pass 1 and the inverse square root, so those names and widths are part of the interface.

rsqrt and requant are separate modules supplied as source files, not something to write. Instantiate them with exactly these ports, connected by name: rsqrt (input clk, input rst_n, input [29:0] x, input valid_in, output [16:0] y, output [4:0] e, output valid_out); requant (input clk, input rst_n, input signed [28:0] acc_in, input [17:0] scale, input [6:0] shift, input valid_in, output signed [7:0] q_out, output sat, output valid_out). rsqrt has a latency of 3 cycles and requant of exactly 9.
All state resets to zero: busy and o_valid are 0 during reset.
